title: Njoroge v Kamau (Land) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Dispute over a title deed in Kiambu alleged to have been obtained by fraud. The court held that a title obtained through a forged transfer is liable to cancellation under section 26 of the Land Registration Act, and that the registered proprietor cannot rely on the indefeasibility of title where fraud is proved to the required standard, higher than a balance of probabilities.

The court considered the pleadings, the evidence adduced and the submissions of counsel. It is trite law that the burden of proof lies with the party who alleges. title: Wanjiru v Registrar of Titles (Land) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Appeal on cancellation of a fraudulent title. The Court of Appeal affirmed that particulars of fraud must be specifically pleaded and strictly proved, and that an innocent purchaser for value without notice may retain title.

The court considered the pleadings, the evidence adduced and the submissions of counsel. It is trite law that the burden of proof lies with the party who alleges. title: Otieno v Kenya Breweries (Employment) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Claim for unfair termination. The employer failed to give the employee a hearing before dismissal contrary to section 41 of the Employment Act, 2007. The court awarded compensation equivalent to six months gross salary and notice pay.

The court considered the pleadings, the evidence adduced and the submissions of counsel. It is trite law that the burden of proof lies with the party who alleges. Claim for unfair termination. title: Mutua v Bidco (Employment) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Procedural fairness in dismissal: the employer must notify the employee of the grounds, allow a companion at the hearing and consider representations. Substantive justification alone does not cure a procedurally unfair termination.

The court considered the pleadings, the evidence adduced and the submissions of counsel. It is trite law that the burden of proof lies with the party who alleges. title: Hassan v Republic (Criminal) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Bail pending trial. Article 49(1)(h) of the Constitution entitles an arrested person to be released on bond or bail unless there are compelling reasons. The court weighed flight risk and the likelihood of interference with witnesses.

title: Republic v Karanja (Criminal) [SYNTHETIC]
text:

title: Cheruiyot v Equity Bank (Contract) [SYNTHETIC]
text:
Enforceability of a penal interest clause in a loan agreement. The court held that a clause operating as a penalty rather than a genuine pre-estimate of loss is unenforceable, and the borrower was entitled to relief.

The court considered the pleadings, the evidence adduced and the submissions of counsel. It is trite law that the burden of proof lies with the party who alleges.
